Jing: Heads-up — HF -> Redwood conversion for a llama-chat bring-up hit a nasty special-token/token-id drift. Model runs show embedding-size mismatch and generation gets truncated or emits <unk> frequently.
Alex: Can you paste a minimal repro + the tokenizer files?
Jing: Quick repro notes: used AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/user-llama-chat-7b') then ran our redwood-hf-convert tool pointing at the tokenizer dir. After conversion runtime logs: "Embedding matrix size 32002 vs vocab_size 32000" and some prompts produce repeated <unk> or missing BOS so the chat system prompt never attaches.
Jing: Quick local checks I ran:
```
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/user-llama-chat-7b')
print(t.special_tokens_map)
print(len(t))
print(t.get_vocab().get('', None))
```
Jing: What I traced: the HF tokenizer had an added_tokens.json that listed two custom tokens (one was '' duplicated in different formats, plus '<|instruction|>'). When redwood-hf-convert merges tokenizer.json + added_tokens.json it ended up inserting the new tokens ahead of the end of vocab which shifted subsequent token IDs by +2, but the model config.json still had the old vocab_size (32000). So embedding lookup was misaligned.
Maria: Oof. Symptoms align with the eval failures we saw: system role gets concatenated without BOS, sampling produces junk tokens, and quantized loads fail with index OOB or shape mismatch.
Alex: Short workaround that helped me locally: add the special tokens to the tokenizer and resize the model embeddings before export. Example:
```
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/user-llama-chat-7b')
tok.add_special_tokens({'bos_token':'<s>', 'eos_token':'</s>'})
tok.add_tokens(['<|instruction|>'])  # ensure added token is in vocab
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('hf/user-llama-chat-7b')
model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tok))
tok.save_pretrained('./fixed_tok')
model.save_pretrained('./fixed_model')
```
Alex: Key is: update tokenizer vocab *and* model embedding size together, and make sure config.json.vocab_size matches len(tok).
Oliver: Additional note: HF stores different pieces — special_tokens_map.json, added_tokens.json, tokenizer.json, vocab.json. If you merge or canonicalize them out of order you can end up with inconsistent ID assignments. Our converter should canonicalize: load tokenizer with transformers, call tokenizer.add_tokens/add_special_tokens as needed, then save_pretrained and read back the finalized vocab size.
Oliver: I'll open a PR to redwood-hf-convert to validate (a) assert model.config.vocab_size == len(tokenizer), (b) on mismatch either auto-resize the model or fail with a clear mapping file old_id->new_id.
release-bot: deploy job #452 queued for redwood-hf-convert (staging).
Maria: On the eval side I'll add a small regression test: tokenize a set of canonical control prompts (system + user) with the HF tokenizer and with the converted tokenizer and compare ID sequences; any deviation should be flagged as a token-id drift. That should catch these edge-cases before infra rollout.
Alex: Quick patch we used earlier: if embedding_size != vocab_size then fail the conversion and emit a .token_id_map.json that lists original_token->converted_token_id so we can remap any stored prompt tokens.
Jing: For now I'll upload the problematic added_tokens.json + tokenizer diffs to the thread. TL;DR: ensure tokenizer.save_pretrained writes the canonicalized tokenizer (no duplicates), added_tokens are applied before computing vocab_size, and update config.json/vocab_size or resize embeddings.
Maria: Also note quantization runs will crash unpredictably if IDs shifted (INT8 paths assume exact indices). I'll pause quant experiments until converter PR lands.
Alex: Thanks — ping me once you upload files, I'll run the id-diff test locally.
Jing: uploading now to /scratch/tokenizer-diffs.tar.gz and linking in the ticket.
